text:
Jess: Heads-up — onboarding mcodebert-small-v2. I pushed weights and a tokenizer artifact but seeing weird BOS/EOS behavior with our chat templates. Can someone do a quick sanity check before I flip the serving config? :eyes:

Raj: Ping — where are the weights and sample failing prompt?

Jess: weights_path: s3://redwood-models/onboard/mcodebert-small-v2/2026-03-17/
sha256: abcdef1234567890deadbeef
serving_config (draft):
```
model: mcodebert-small-v2
tokenizer: mcodebert-bpe
bos_token: "<s>"
eos_token: "</s>"
pad_token: "<pad>"
preserve_bos: false   # current default
strip_eos_on_prefix: true
```
Example that fails locally:
```py
>>> tokenizer.encode("<s>Hello")
[0, 154, 23, 2]  # 0 is <s>
>>> tokenizer.decode([154,23,2])
"Hello</s>"  # BOS dropped, EOS appended unexpectedly
```
This ends up shifting token counts in our chat template (system + user) and breaks prefix KV caching alignment.

Lin: hmm. Can you run the quick tokenizer check script and paste output? Also include vocab[0..5] mapping.

Jess: running now — output: 
```
$ python -m tools.token_check --model-dir s3://redwood-models/onboard/mcodebert-small-v2/2026-03-17/ --show-vocab 0 6
token_map[0] = "<s>"
token_map[1] = "<pad>"
token_map[2] = "</s>"
token_map[3] = " the"
token_map[4] = " of"
token_map[5] = " a"
encode('<s>Hello') -> [0, 154, 23, 2]
decode([0,154,23,2]) -> "<s>Hello</s>"
decode([154,23,2]) -> "Hello</s>"
```
So the tokenizer itself keeps <s> when decoding, but our local glue strips leading tokens for prefix caching path, and then downstream decode is showing trailing EOS injected by the library when a sentence doesn't start with BOS.

Eva: could be interaction with quantized kernel that expects stripped prefixes. On Dedicated we have a flag `preserve_bos` in the serving runtime that defaults to false for some perf reasons. If you want canonical chat semantics set `preserve_bos: true` and `strip_eos_on_prefix: false` in the model config. That will add a tiny latency hit but keeps token counts stable.

Raj: can you try toggling preserve_bos locally and re-run the token_check? Also post the minimal repro prompt you used (exact chat template).

Jess: repro template (exact):
```
[system] "You are an assistant."
[user] "Hello"
```
With current server config the encoded sequence for the request becomes (after our prefix trim step): [154,23,2] and the runtime appends an EOS token later, which makes the caching offsets mismatch by 1. If I flip preserve_bos=true locally I get:
```
encode(full_prompt) -> [0, 154, 23, 2]
serving-prefix-slice -> [0,154]  # preserved
kv-offsets aligned -> OK
```

WeightsBot: Weights uploaded: s3://redwood-models/onboard/mcodebert-small-v2/2026-03-17/ checksum OK (abc...ef) :white_check_mark:

Raj: Ok makes sense. Small config nit: set pad_token to "<|pad|>" to match other onboarded models (helps with batching heuristics). Otherwise LGTM for canary.

Jess: noted, will change pad_token and set preserve_bos: true + strip_eos_on_prefix: false for canary. Will file a tiny patch to serving config and kick a canary roll tonight. Filing PR: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/serving-configs/pull/4321 — pinging for reviews.

Lin: please add a regression unit test that asserts token counts for the system+user template (just a 2-line test).

Jess: will add test in the PR and include the token_check output as an integration artifact. Thanks all :raised_hands:

Raj: thx — will review PR in the morning.

Eva: noted for Dedicated rollout notes — we may want to add a doc blurb about perf/regression tradeoff when preserve_bos toggles.

Jess: yep, I'll add a short note to the model onboarding checklist.
